entities.name: Cuthbert
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cuthbert was a saint of the early Northumbrian church in the Celtic tradition. Born in unknown circumstances, he became a monk, bishop, and hermit, associated with the monasteries of Melrose and Lindisfarne in the Kingdom of Northumbria, today in north-eastern England and south-eastern Scotland.

During his life, Cuthbert was known for his piety and spiritual guidance, which attracted many followers. After his death on March 23, 687, a cult centered around his tomb at Durham Cathedral emerged, making him a popular medieval saint of Northern England. Cuthbert is regarded as the patron saint of Northumbria, with his feast days celebrated on March 20.

Cuthbert's legacy extends beyond his religious influence, as he played a significant role in shaping the cultural and historical identity of the region. His association with the monasteries of Melrose and Lindisfarne helped establish the Kingdom of Northumbria as a major power in medieval England.
